name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
summary: A static upper-body stretch that increases posterior shoulder mobility by drawing one arm horizontally across the chest.

setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and relax your shoulders downward.
Bring one arm straight across your chest at roughly shoulder height.
steps: Hook your opposite forearm or hand around the upper arm or elbow of the extended arm.
Gently pull the arm closer toward your chest until a comfortable stretch is felt in the back of the shoulder.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing.
Release slowly and repeat on the opposite arm.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, using each exhalation to relax deeper into the stretch.
cues: Keep the shoulder blade down away from the ear.
Draw the arm in gently rather than cranking it.
Maintain a tall, upright spine without twisting the torso.

common_faults.fault: Shrugging the shoulder of the stretched arm upward toward the ear.
common_faults.correction: Actively depress the shoulder girdle and keep the shoulder down before applying tension.

common_faults.fault: Twisting the torso to follow the arm across the body.
common_faults.correction: Keep the chest and hips facing square to the front so the stretch isolates the shoulder.

precautions: Avoid aggressive pulling if you experience sharp anterior shoulder pain or impingement symptoms.
